thread:
Alex: heads up — saw a sharp 99th pct latency spike on shared-gpu-pool-c last night (02:15-02:22 UTC). baseline tails went from ~120ms -> 900ms for small gen workloads. anyone else see this?
Maria: yup, noticed. timeline shows a kernel selection flip to the generic path and KV cache miss rate jumped ~x7. batching heuristic also dropped to single-request batches during the window.
Jon: adding the perf snapshot link: https://dash.redwood/example/pool-c/1797777 (redacted) — flame graph attached in the alert.
infra-bot: [ALERT] pool-c latency anomaly detected. sample_count=6000, p99=912ms, p50=78ms. auto-sampling triggered.
Maria: quick log excerpt:```
[02:15:12] kernel_autotuner: switching from optimized_matmul to fallback_generic for model:opt-lr-7b
[02:15:14] kv_cache: evict slot_count=124 -> 204, evictions=418
[02:15:15] batching: heuristic.window=8 -> 1, dispatch_batch_size=1
```
Alex: interesting that autotuner flipped. could be due to memory pressure or a bad fingerprint from a long-seq tenant. any tenant spikes around then?
Tien: correlating traces now — tenant-omega had a burst of 12k short requests (seq_len median 1024) between 02:14:50-02:16:30. they were marked as high-priority and pinned to pool-c.
Eva: that long-seq pattern could have inflated KV footprint causing evictions for other tenants; when KV misses happen our kernel chooser falls back to safer kernels which are slower.
Jon: attached pprof sample: hotspots in kv_lookup and fallback_matmul. Also saw GPU mem-bandwidth saturation ~87%.
Maria: hypothesis: tenant-omega's long sequences caused KV thrash -> evictions -> more cache misses -> autotuner flip -> fallback kernel -> batching collapse -> per-request latency tail.
Alex: agreed. temporary mitigations? thoughts: 1) soft QPS cap per-tenant on shared pools, 2) prefer keeping autotuner pinned unless mem pressure sustained, 3) opportunistic KV prefetch/pinning for active tenants.
Tien: I pushed a soft throttle policy to pool-c that limits new sessions per-tenant to 300 rps and marks heavy long-seq requests as lower priority. observing.
infra-bot: [ACTION] soft-throttle applied to pool-c at 02:20:03 by Tien.
Eva: after throttle p99 dropped back to ~140ms within ~40s. initial signs look good. we should still fix root cause behavior.
Jon: next steps for root cause: replay tenant-omega trace in staging with same memory footprint, reproduce autotuner flip, run kernel_selection trace with `--debug-fingerprint`.
Maria: I'll open a perf-regression PR to add a guard in autotuner: require sustained mem_pressure>threshold for N=30s before switching. also add metric for 'kv_eviction_rate' to per-tenant dashboard.
Alex: assign owners: Maria -> autotuner guard PR, Jon -> staging replay + kernel trace, Eva -> dashboard tile, Tien -> follow-up on throttle policy and opt-out for dedicated tenants.
Alex: thanks everyone. please paste any additional logs or short repro commands here. cc @sre-team if we want an incident postmortem. :thumbsup:
Jon: repro command for staging run:```bash
./run_repro --pool=staging-c --trace=tenant-omega-2026-03-17.json --concurrency=120 --seq_len=1024
```
Maria: got it, will start the autotuner test after Jon's replay completes.
Tien: leaving throttle rule in place for 4h and watching. will escalate if it recurs.
Alex: filing an incident note now and linking this thread. thanks all.
